name: server-war-split
description: Refactor the application into independently deployable web and service WARs with REST as the runtime boundary.

tasks.title: Inventory cross-WAR calls and deployment contracts
tasks.description: Trace web-to-service EJB injections, JNDI lookups, REST calls, shared library use, routes, security, persistence units, and deployment assumptions. Identify service-owned behavior consumed by web and external clients.
acceptanceCriteria: Every active web-to-service invocation is listed with its caller, provider, current mechanism, and required behavior.
Existing routes, authentication/authorization rules, persistence units, and deployment context-root assumptions are recorded.
The separate server-admin-authentication role and its exclusion from the future bundle are captured.

tasks.title: Capture baseline behavior for affected workflows
tasks.description: Add or identify focused tests and reproducible checks covering report reads/writes, signee data, student and target-document access, calendar/ticket operations, and report-date lookup.
acceptanceCriteria: Each in-scope workflow has a repeatable baseline test or documented verification procedure.
Error cases and authorization-sensitive behavior are represented, not only successful responses.

tasks.title: Define REST contracts and caller identity behavior
tasks.description: Specify service REST operations for inventoried calls, reusing existing ServiceInternalClient and service endpoints where suitable. Decide how web-to-service authentication, caller identity, authorization, TLS, serialization, and error mapping preserve current semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Every inventoried operation has an existing or proposed REST endpoint and request/response contract.
Caller identity and role propagation are explicit for each security-sensitive operation.
No endpoint contract depends on a shared JVM, EJB reference, or implementation-specific JNDI name.

tasks.title: Implement missing service REST operations
tasks.description: Implement and test service endpoints needed by web but not adequately covered by existing REST APIs, including report operations, calendar/date access, student data, target-document functions, and resource access as established by the inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: All required operations in the approved REST contracts are implemented.
Tests cover serialization, success and failure responses, and security/authorization behavior.
Existing operations are reused rather than duplicated when they already satisfy the contract.

tasks.title: Configure web REST clients securely
tasks.description: Configure REST client destinations, TLS, authentication, providers, logo resource path, and error mapping from runtime configuration. Remove hard-coded service URLs and permissive hostname verification.
acceptanceCriteria: Service destination and security configuration are externally configurable.
TLS hostname validation is not bypassed.
REST client URL validation, hostname verification, and error mapping are verified in the deployment smoke test; no new test infrastructure is added.

tasks.title: Migrate web report and calendar calls to REST
tasks.description: Replace web's report/calendar EJB injections and lookups with REST-backed clients or web-local adapters. Cover report reads and writes, calendar dates, report lookup, notes, markers, and custom values as identified by inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: Affected report and calendar workflows pass the baseline checks using REST, including batch note/marker reads.
Ambiguous-date behavior and write failures remain explicit and behaviorally compatible.
No service-owned report/calendar EJB is directly injected or looked up by web.

tasks.title: Migrate web student and document calls to REST
tasks.description: Replace web's direct student, target-document, signee, and other inventoried service bean calls with REST. Replace service-owned AppResourcesContext or similar JNDI access with a supported boundary operation where required.
acceptanceCriteria: Affected student, signee, and target-document workflows pass their baseline checks through REST.
Service-owned EJB and implementation-specific JNDI calls are removed from web for these operations.
Shared domain types and utilities may remain in sphairas-server-libs without creating a runtime invocation dependency.

tasks.title: Verify web has no in-process service dependency
tasks.description: Search and validate the web module for remaining service-owned EJB injection, global JNDI lookup, or other cross-module invocation. Resolve active findings and document any unrelated or inactive references.
acceptanceCriteria: No active web-to-service business call uses EJB injection, service implementation JNDI, or shared-JVM assumptions.
All remaining service calls use the approved REST clients.
The web module builds and affected behavior tests pass.

tasks.title: Convert persistence and calendar modules to JARs
tasks.description: Change server-persistence and server-calendar packaging to ordinary JARs and add them as runtime dependencies of server-service. Inspect schema-generation settings and determine safe production behavior before deployment.
acceptanceCriteria: Both modules build as ordinary JAR artifacts and are included in the service WAR runtime.
Persistence-unit names, datasource bindings, entity discovery, CDI/EJB discovery, and transaction behavior are verified.
Schema-generation settings are reviewed and no accidental destructive schema action is introduced.

tasks.title: Integrate calendar resources into service WAR
tasks.description: Move or merge calendar REST resources, servlet mappings, descriptors, security configuration, and required resources into the service deployment. Publish the new calendar URLs and update known clients.
acceptanceCriteria: Calendar, ticket, student, and report-date endpoints are reachable under the service context at the new URLs.
External client configuration is updated or documented for the new URLs; old calendar URLs are not required.
Calendar authorization behavior is preserved and verified.

tasks.title: Make both WAR dependency sets independently deployable
tasks.description: Ensure each WAR packages sphairas-server-libs and its needed runtime dependencies, or document and configure a deliberate server-wide library mechanism. Prefer self-contained WAR dependency packaging.
acceptanceCriteria: The web WAR contains its required shared library dependencies without relying on the service WAR or EAR.
The service WAR contains its required shared library and persistence/calendar dependencies without relying on the web WAR or EAR.
No duplicate or conflicting API classes are introduced into the deployments.

tasks.title: Deploy and verify both WARs independently
tasks.description: Configure standalone context roots and deploy web and service separately on Payara Full. Web keeps its FOP/XSL-FO/logo files in its own app-resources directory (system property sphairas.web.app-resources, default <instanceRoot>/app-resources); the directory must be provisioned for the web deployment. Exercise startup, REST connectivity, authentication, authorization, persistence, messaging/timers, reports, documents, and calendar behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Each WAR deploys and runs without the EAR and without the other WAR's classes or in-process services.
Integration checks pass across the REST boundary for the affected workflows.
The separately deployed server-admin-authentication WAR remains available for its existing parallel authentication role.

tasks.title: Remove EAR assembly and deploy the two-WAR bundle
tasks.description: Remove server-ear from the future reactor/bundle, update Docker and build scripts to deploy server-web and server-service independently, and remove EAR-specific JNDI/context-root assumptions. Keep server-admin-authentication as a separate support deployment outside the bundle.
acceptanceCriteria: The future application bundle deploys server-web and server-service as independent WARs, with no EAR.
Docker/build configuration uses the intended standalone artifacts and context roots.
server-admin-authentication is not included in the two-WAR bundle and its existing support role is not silently removed.

tasks.title: Validate split acceptance criteria and document deferred migration
tasks.description: Run the final build and integration checks against the independently deployed bundle. Record evidence for the REST-only boundary and explicitly keep MicroProfile-only runtime migration and UI technology replacement out of scope.
acceptanceCriteria: All plan acceptance criteria for the Payara Full two-WAR split are verified.
No unintended schema recreation occurs.
The current UI technology remains unchanged.
MicroProfile-only migration is recorded as a separate future major effort, not represented as completed by EAR removal.
